changelog.change: TESSERA_BF16_K1 stops being unattested: attested_rungs_q256 [1792] (R=7, the rung the receipt served) and two sm_121 dense cells, decode and batch, both bf16_unquantized on torch.mm with the row scale as an fp32 epilogue. The receipt is docs/measurements/tessera-bf16-route-served-2026-09-02.md: four route censuses on the pinned image -- resident/eager, resident/compiled, streamed/eager, streamed/compiled -- each recording all 112 declared modules on the TESSERA_BF16 route with decoder torch_window in BOTH the prefill and the decode shape and zero problems, plus a served KL-vs-BF16 in both residency modes on the Qwen-tokenized n=8 x 512 corpus against the image-matched teacher, with the folded stock twin on vanilla vLLM as the control. route_status is backed_with_serve_flag because the residency is selected by TESSERA_SERVE_MODE and both values were served; qualification is device_qualified because the censuses ran on this GB10 (sm_121, capability [12, 1]), not on a table. Nothing wider is attested: one rung, one platform, dense structure only, no routed-MoE cell, and tensor_parallel.units still caps this family at max_world_size 1.

Third family: TESSERA_BF16_K1, the scalar BF16 grid over the CHANNEL plane and the same window body the E4M3 family ships, decoded to a plain bf16 tile and served W16A16 through the stock BF16 GEMM (activation contract bf16_unquantized -- a value, because a gate must be able to tell 'unquantised by design' from 'nobody filled it in'). It exists because the E4M3 ALPHABET floors the window body at ~0.022 out-space from R=6 upward while the identical trellis over bf16 keeps halving at ~1.93x per bit, so above ~6 bpp an 8-bit tile has nothing left to buy. reader_rate_range_q256 is [256, 4096] continuous at step 1, DERIVED the way E4M3's was in v2 -- 25 candidate rungs (every integer rate 1..16 plus nine non-integer rungs of the kind a Bresenham schedule makes: 300, 777, 779, 1000, 1023, 1500, 2047, 2500, 4095) encoded and taken through the route's own load path, parse -> shard -> prepare including the element-for-element cross-check against tessera.decode.materialize_bf16 (experiments/bf16_reader_rate_range.py). 4096 is the grammar's shaped domain (code rate 1..16 over a 16-bit alphabet) and the sweep reaches it: the recipe widens the window table to max(14, rate) above R=14 rather than refusing, and L=15 and L=16 both load. The only candidate refused was q256=777 over 128 columns, and that is a GEOMETRY refusal ('it needs 9/2 columns at rate 4') not a rate one -- it loads at 512 columns, so it does not bound the range. attested_rungs_q256 is EMPTY and there is no lane_eligibility cell: no container receipt covers this family yet -- no served census and no served KL against the plain-BF16 twin the exporter writes -- so every BF16 rung resolves unattested, which is the honest status and not a refusal. A cell is added when a receipt exists. Additive: a v1/v2 reader that does not know this family simply does not match it. tensor_parallel gains a TESSERA_BF16_K1 unit at max_world_size 1, the same refusal the other two families carry: a Tessera unit is one blob per vLLM module against a shared rate schedule, so a sharded form needs per-rank wires and not a byte range.

reader_rate_range_q256 now states what the DECODER accepts, measured by encoding a unit at each candidate rate and running it through the route's own load path; the plugin refuses a declared q256 outside it (it did not before, and an allocated checkpoint carrying seven unlisted rungs served with nothing refusing). E4M3 widened from [1024,1024] to [256,2048] continuous at step 1 -- the bound is the trellis grammar's shaped domain (code rate 1..8 over an 8-bit-native alphabet), not the rungs anyone had exported. E2M1x2 stays the single point 896, bounded BELOW by the native decoder (span-2 TCQ only; the sub-cap WINDOW body has no served decode) and ABOVE by the same grammar (rate 7 of arity-2 native 8). candidate_rungs_q256 renamed attested_rungs_q256 because it never was the decodable set and reading it as one is how the gap opened: it is the rungs a lane_eligibility cell attests. Added an explicit grid to each entry so a (route, grid) pair with no published range refuses rather than resolving to another entry's numbers. candidate_rungs_q256 is retained as a DEPRECATED ALIAS of attested_rungs_q256 -- same list, refused if it disagrees -- so this stays an ADDITIVE change that a v1 reader can still read, which is why the schema string does not move. It is dropped at schema v2.
First published contract: two dense families, four cells, TP1/EP0.
